title: The sultan's demand
hookLine: Namdev sings of a sultan who demanded a miracle, and of the Lord who saved him (Bhairao, Namdev)

cards: Prove it. Two words that can corner anyone. Show me your God does something, right here, right now, or else.
In one of his hymns, Namdev tells of the day a ruler said exactly that to him. Not a friend teasing, but a sultan, with power behind the words and Namdev's life on the table.
The printer who sang that everything is Gobind is suddenly asked to make Gobind perform.

teach.h: LET ME SEE YOUR LORD'S WORKS.
teach.b: The hymn is in Raag Bhairao, around Ang 1165. In paraphrase: the sultan says, listen, Namdev, let me see the works of your Lord. He has Namdev bound, and a dead cow is set before him.
Bring this cow back to life, says the sultan, or I'll cut off your head right here. Now Namdev's answer, the heart of the day. How can this be?
Nothing happens by my doing. Whatever the Lord does, that is what happens. He won't put on a show, or claim a power that isn't his.
And he won't drop the Lord to save his neck either.

The hymn holds him right there, under threat, honest about what he can and can't do. Then the turn. The hymn says the Lord came to Namdev's side, the cow rose up, and the sultan, shaken, came asking forgiveness.
It tells the rescue quickly. It lingers longer on the moment before, when Namdev had nothing to offer but the truth.
And look where the hymn puts the credit. Not on Namdev. He refused to be the miracle worker the sultan wanted.
He stayed a devotee, and the saving came from beyond him. That's why today's line has two halves.
Namdev was saved. He was never shown off.

how: Namdev's hymn of the sultan is sung as gurbani, and Sikhs often recall it alongside the Gurus' teaching that devotees should not seek to display miraculous powers.

o: a soldier who guarded the temple door through the night
the ruler who told Namdev to raise a dead cow or die
a rich merchant who bought Namdev's printed cloth

games.q: inside the hymn — tap the pairs.
p: let me see your Lord's works

s: Namdev agrees to perform a miracle to save himself
he says nothing happens by his doing; whatever the Lord does happens.
the sultan's demand is told in a hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib
it's in Raag Bhairao, among Namdev's hymns.

games.q: you're bound before a ruler who says: raise this dead cow, or lose your head. what do you say?
o: I'll do it, just give me time.
nothing happens by my doing; whatever the Lord does happens.
I renounce my Lord; let me go.
games.why: Namdev refuses both the show and the surrender. the hymn says the Lord came to his side, and the cow rose.

practice: Bring to mind one place in your life where someone wants you to perform: prove you're right, prove you're good enough, say what they want to hear.

Notice where that pressure sits in your body, breathe out slowly, and let one honest sentence form: this is what I can do, and this is what I can't. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you breathe out.

wordCard.voice: Sultan. The ruler who ordered Namdev to raise a dead cow or die, and heard him say: nothing happens by my doing.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sultan, the ruler who makes the demand in Namdev's hymn.

carryVoice: Your line: saved, not shown. Namdev stayed honest, and the credit went beyond him. See you tomorrow.
